candidate_title: Predicting Inductive Biases of Pre-Trained Models

review_output.decision_rationale: The full text explicitly studies Transformer-based pre-trained language models including BERT, RoBERTa, T5, and GPT-2, and it empirically evaluates syntactic phenomena such as subject-verb agreement, negative polarity items, and filler-gap dependencies. Although the paper also includes synthetic and GloVe/LSTM comparisons, the study clearly includes and analyzes Transformer language models with empirical syntax-focused experiments, satisfying both required inclusion criteria.

support_spans.quote: We focus on three syntactic phenomena
The Subject-Verb Agreement (SVA) construction requires detecting whether the verb agrees in number with its subject
The Negative Polarity Items (NPI) construction requires detecting whether a negative polarity item (e.g., “any”, “ever”) is grammatical in a given context
The Filler-Gap Dependencies (GAP) construction requires detecting whether a sentence containing a gap is grammatical
For each (s, t) feature pair, we plot the use of the spurious feature (s-only error) as a function of the evidence against the spurious feature seen in training (s-only example rate).
